q: A note states that the amendment capping the Council of Ministers also created the economic reservation. Which statement is correct?
options: The two changes belong to different amendments, in 2003 and 2019 respectively
The two changes belong to the same amendment, enacted in 2003
The two changes belong to the same amendment, enacted in 2019
The two changes belong to different amendments, in 2003 and 2021 respectively
expl: The ministerial cap came in 2003 and the economic reservation in 2019.
why: The fourth option separates the two changes correctly and misdates the second, which is the finer error.
trapnote: Separating two changes is only half the task. The dates must also be right.

q: A note correctly states that the voting age is eighteen and adds that the schooling right applies from eighteen to twenty-five. Which statement is correct?
options: Both limbs are right, the schooling right having been extended in 2002
The first limb is wrong and the second right: the voting age is twenty-one
Both limbs are wrong: the voting age is twenty-one and schooling covers six to fourteen
The first limb is right and the second wrong: the schooling right covers six to fourteen
expl: A true first limb carries a false second limb.
why: Half-truth construction, with the accurate opening lending credibility to what follows.
trapnote: An accurate first limb is frequently there to carry an inaccurate second one.

q: Consider a claim that the 2024 ruling on community resources permits acquisition without compensation. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim succeeds: the ruling dispensed with compensation for community resources
The claim fails: the ruling widened the directive but preserved compensation
The claim fails: the ruling narrowed the directive and did not touch compensation
The claim succeeds where the State records a public purpose in the acquisition order
expl: The ruling narrowed the directive and said nothing dispensing with compensation.
why: The third option misdescribes the direction of the ruling while reaching the right conclusion.
trapnote: A right conclusion drawn from a misdescribed holding is still a wrong option.

q: A college declines to implement the economic reservation, citing a pending challenge. Which statement is correct?
options: The challenge remains pending before a larger bench of the Supreme Court
The challenge was decided in 2022 and the amendment was upheld
The challenge was decided in 2022 and the amendment was struck down
The challenge was withdrawn and the amendment has never been tested
expl: The amendment was upheld by a majority in November 2022.
why: The second option borrows the pending-reference pattern from a different and unrelated controversy.
trapnote: That challenge was decided. A pending larger-bench reference belongs to a different subject.

q: Consider the position of a Council of Ministers in a State with a sixty-member Assembly: 1-The ceiling is fifteen per cent. 2-The floor is twelve ministers. 3-The ceiling prevails over the floor. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The floor operates where fifteen per cent would yield fewer than twelve.
why: Fifteen per cent of sixty is nine, so the floor of twelve governs and the ceiling does not prevail.
trapnote: In small Assemblies the floor governs. The ceiling binds only where it yields the larger figure.

q: It is claimed that the 2022 district reorganisation in Andhra Pradesh required a constitutional amendment. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim succeeds: alteration of internal boundaries requires an amendment
The claim fails: such reorganisation requires a law of Parliament instead
The claim succeeds: any change to a State's administration requires ratification
The claim fails: creation of districts within a State is done under State law
expl: Districts are administrative units created under State law.
why: The third option confuses internal districts with the alteration of State boundaries, which is a different subject.
trapnote: Districts are State administrative units. Altering State boundaries is a different process entirely.

q: Consider the special provisions for Andhra Pradesh: 1-They were inserted by the 32nd amendment. 2-They followed a political settlement of 1973. 3-They are exercised through an order made in 1975. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: All three are accurate and describe a single sequence.
why: The settlement preceded the amendment, and the order followed it, which is the order of events to retain.
trapnote: Settlement, then amendment, then order. The sequence runs in that direction only.

q: A claim is made that the criminal statutes in force from July 2024 required a constitutional amendment to enact. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim succeeds: replacing the penal code required an amendment
The claim fails: they are ordinary legislation enacted under the existing lists
The claim fails: they were enacted by ordinance and later ratified
The claim succeeds: criminal law was moved to the Union List by amendment
expl: Criminal law and procedure are existing subjects; ordinary legislation sufficed.
why: The fourth option invents a transfer between Lists, which would itself have required ratification.
trapnote: Replacing a statute needs a statute. Only a change to the Constitution needs an amendment.

q: Consider: 1-The 2020 amendment extended seat reservation to 2030. 2-The 2023 amendment added reservation for women. 3-Both operate on the same articles. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The 2023 amendment inserted new articles rather than operating on the existing ones.
why: The distinction between amending an existing article and inserting a new one is the point being tested.
trapnote: New reservations usually arrive as new articles rather than amendments to existing ones.

q: It is claimed that the ceiling on reservation was abolished by the 2022 decision. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim is accurate: the ceiling no longer operates in any context
The claim understates it: the decision also abolished backward-class reservation
The claim is inaccurate: the decision reaffirmed the ceiling for all categories
The claim overstates it: the ceiling is not a basic feature and the economic quota sits outside it
expl: The ceiling continues to govern backward-class reservation; the economic quota was placed outside it.
why: The difference between abolishing a rule and confining it is the distinction the item tests.
trapnote: The ceiling was confined, not abolished. It still binds the backward-class compartment.
